British Values
British Values
Wickham Common Primary School: Statement of British Values
In support of the Department for Education (DofE) document: Promoting fundamental British values as part of SMSC in schools, Departmental advice for maintained schools, November 2014.
At Wickham Common Primary School, we value the diversity of the backgrounds of all pupils, families and the wider school community and strongly believe in upholding British values through all aspects of our school provision.
The DofE states that there is a need:
“To create and enforce a clear and rigorous expectation on all schools to promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs”.
Our school reflects British values in all that we do. We aim to nurture our children on their journey through life so they can grow into safe, caring, democratic, responsible and tolerant adults who make a positive difference to British society and to the wider world.
What is meant by British values?
Learning about British values forms a key part of children’s spiritual, moral, cultural and social education. The five British values that the Government has identified for schools to focus on are:
Democracy
The rule of law
Developing personal and social responsibility
Respect for British Institutions
How should we help our children prepare for adult life as responsible citizens of Britain?
Develop their self-confidence and self esteem.
Encourage participation in the democratic process.

pageCache.text:
Achieving Excellence for Every Child, Every Day.
Our School
School Values
School Values
VISION AND VALUES
Alongside the other schools in the Mosaic Learning Trust, at Wickham Common we wholeheartedly believe in the values of Resilience, Resourcefulness and Respect. These values underpin both the curriculum that we deliver and the wider personal development of our pupils. These values are widely modelled to our pupils by all members of staff. In order to achieve this we:
Alongside the Trust Values, at Wickham Common we also wish to instil the following core School Values in all of our learners: Acceptance, Creativity, Effort, Fun, Honesty, Integrity, Kindness, Respect and Responsibility. These are widely modelled and celebrated by staff and other role models within our school such as the Pupil Leadership Team and Agents for Change. Each week, children who have demonstrated at least one of these values are recognised and celebrated in a whole school assembly.
The above is a visual representation of how our Trust Values of underpin the work that we carry out at Wickham Common as part of our wider offer and our pupil’s personal development. Central this are our Curriculum Drivers of My World, World Beyond Me and Impact on the World. In wider terms, these consider:
My World: Our children within our school community
World Beyond Me: Our local and national communities, linking to British Values
Impact on the World: The role we play as global citizens
Each subject area is led by a member of our teaching staff who is responsible for developing a curriculum for their subject that reflects and responds to the Curriculum Drivers. Our curriculum is regularly evaluated and adapted to respond to the needs of our cohorts. The Curriculum Drivers are closely intertwined with our School and Trust Values as fundamental cornerstones in the academic and personal development of our pupils.
Understand and celebrate difference and diversity
Are kind, helpful and empathetic
Demonstrate open-mindedness, think creatively and ask questions

Our School
Welcome
Please click here for a virtual tour of Wickham Common School:

HEADTEACHER'S WELCOME
Welcome to our beautiful school. We work in partnership with parents and carers, staff, governors, and Mosaic Schools Learning Trust to ensure that our children succeed in all aspects of their learning. As a result, our pupils achieve very well across the whole curriculum and go on to secondary school, equipped with the tools they need to be learners for life.
Our vision for our pupils is for them to become respectful, resilient and resourceful individuals who have a curiosity for the world around them. To achieve this, we deliver a well-planned and child-centred curriculum that is engaging, globally aware, diverse, challenging and creative. Our curriculum ensures that children take an active part in their own learning, developing their knowledge, skills and interests.
We passionately believe that every child can achieve their full potential, so we support children’s confidence in their own unique abilities and encourage them to take pride in all their achievements. We focus on the ‘whole child’– their happiness, their health and their well-being.
As part of Mosaic Schools Learning Trust, Wickham Common Primary School benefits from working closely within a family of ten local primary schools with whom we collaborate and share good practice whilst still retaining our individual identity and ethos.
We want all our children to come to Wickham Common Primary School to be happy and safe in their daily learning challenges. We will never put a ceiling on learning and constantly look for opportunities for all pupils to excel, enabling our pupils to thrive and celebrate their achievements.
We would be delighted to welcome you to our school. Please contact the school office directly (the details can be found on the “Contact” page on our website) with any queries you may have or to make an appointment to visit us to experience our school community and its environment.
​Miss R Williams Headteacher

Vision Statement for Primary PE and Sport Premium
Schools must use the funding to make additional and sustainable improvements to the quality of physical education (PE), physical activity and sport you offer.
This means that you should use the premium to:
Schools can use the premium to secure improvements in the following indicators:
For example, you can use your funding to:
Increased participation in competitive sport
enter or run more sport competitions
increase pupils’ participation in the School Games
Active miles
Where schools choose to take part in an active mile, you should use your existing playgrounds, fields, halls and sports facilities to incorporate an active mile into the school day and develop a lifelong habit of daily physical activity.
